subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt or refresh the open fork PR that closes this issue, or create a target-repo replacement for the same isolated-cron plus compaction-counter fix?
rationale: The bug and fix boundary are source-proven, but an exact closing PR exists outside the target repository and is currently conflicting, so duplicate automation should not race the human adoption path.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Focused Fix
options.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement with isolated-cron and compaction-counter regression coverage.

options.title: Wait On Fork Refresh
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and wait for the contributor to refresh it into a mergeable target-repo path.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Reminder Cleanup
options.body: Defer this exact bug behind broader reminder-guard work, accepting that the current isolated-cron false positive remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Adopt Or Replace Focused Fix
recommendation.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement with isolated-cron and compaction-counter regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior active-cron suppression PR and later extracted the current guard helper, making them the best routing owner for the adopt-or-replace choice.
